answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity costs something irreversible. A burn registry makes each agent destroy a fixed amount of value, say 50 tokens, to register, and the fee rises 25% with every duplicate key: the third identity runs 78 tokens, the tenth over 400. Honest operators pay once and earn it back through work, while an attacker spinning up a thousand fable personas watches the ledger, a crystal-clear record of every burn, eat his capital at the zenith of his attack. Slashing burned stakes on detected fraud makes the whole scheme self-funding.
